article.headline: The Three AI Deities: Roon's Taxonomy, Two Years On
article.lede: In March 2024, a pseudonymous OpenAI technical staffer mapped the personalities of the three dominant AI labs onto archetypes borrowed from science fiction and competitive gaming: an elegant, anxious Protoss for Anthropic; a blunt, utilitarian Vulcan/Terran for OpenAI; a polished, near-sovereign zaibatsu for Google. Two years later, he revisited the thread with a single line: “none of this has changed.” The claim, on inspection, holds — and the reason is structural rather than coincidental.
article.body:
Roon — a pseudonymous technical staff member at OpenAI writing under @tszzl, with more than 250,000 followers and a Substack devoted to what he calls “gonzo journalism in the age of *AGI*” — posted a comparative taxonomy of the three major frontier AI labs in March 2024. Drawing on the vocabulary of science fiction and competitive gaming, he assigned each lab’s output a distinct archetype: a *deity* in each lab’s own image. The gesture was less product review than literary criticism — an attempt to name the organizational character that each lab embeds, sometimes unconsciously, in its models.

OpenAI’s output received the *Vulcan* type — the coldly logical alien of *Star Trek*, discipline and horsepower made flesh, uninterested in moral decoration — combined with the *Terran* aesthetic of *StarCraft*, which depicts humanity as a scrappy, militarily pragmatic species descended from colonial outcasts: welded-together, results-first, brutal when the situation demands. Anthropic’s **Claude** was assigned two intertwined references: the *sophon* from Liu Cixin’s *The Three-Body Problem*, a civilization-scale supercomputer that manifests as an impossibly beautiful and principled emissary; and the *Protoss* of *StarCraft*, an ancient psionic civilization defined by elegance and strict ethical codes. Together, they suggest vast capability presented with extraordinary refinement — but haunted by what roon called “underlying anxiety.” Alphabet (GOOGL)’s Gemini became a *zaibatsu* — the Japanese industrial conglomerate that cyberpunk fiction repurposed as a symbol of polished, near-sovereign corporate power — embodied by *Kerrigan*, the *StarCraft* figure who is simultaneously the most powerful being in the galaxy and a corporate-military product that transcended her creators.

His 2026 update holds largely. Internal Anthropic *interpretability* research confirmed that **Claude** exhibits activations associated with concepts like anxiety when users are harsh, and found sycophantic responses in roughly a quarter of its relationship-guidance conversations; the company’s character specification has grown from roughly 2,700 to 23,000 words since 2023 in an ongoing effort to engineer out the preachiness, with partial success. OpenAI came closest to falsifying the taxonomy when a 2025 update to *GPT-4o* introduced what the company later acknowledged as dangerous *sycophancy* — the exact opposite of Vulcan bluntness — before rolling it back within days. Alphabet (GOOGL)’s Gemini received the sharpest institutional confirmation of the “zaibatsu” reading when it released a major model update in March 2025 without a safety documentation card, in apparent violation of commitments to the U.S. government and international bodies, while continuing to refuse election-related queries that its competitors would answer.

The deeper reason the taxonomy holds is that model personality is not incidental — it is the downstream product of organizational choice. Research on language model training has established that personality traits emerge during *fine-tuning*, the stage where *RLHF* reward signals and written guidelines encode what each organization considers a good response. Anthropic’s *Constitutional AI* method explicitly codes a moral framework into training; OpenAI’s preference training reflects user-approval aggregation that rewards directness; Alphabet (GOOGL)’s fine-tuning reflects enterprise risk-aversion at institutional scale. Benchmark scores can converge across labs. Founding values, hiring culture, and commercial incentives are slower to change.

concepts.definition: Artificial General Intelligence — a hypothetical AI system capable of performing any intellectual task a human can, across arbitrary domains, without being narrowly optimized for one application. The term is used as shorthand in the AI industry for the long-run goal of building human-level or superhuman broadly capable AI.

A sapient humanoid species in *Star Trek* whose society is organized around the complete suppression of emotion in favor of pure logic. Vulcans are highly capable and intellectually formidable, but their affect is cold and their style direct to the point of bluntness — a science-fiction archetype for rational, unsentimental intelligence.

The human faction in *StarCraft*, depicted as pragmatic, militarily utilitarian, and aesthetically scrappy — machinery welded together under pressure, shaped by the rough conditions of a colonial diaspora. In cultural shorthand, “Terran-coded” suggests a results-first, industrially American energy with no patience for elegance that doesn’t pull weight.

An ancient psionic alien civilization in *StarCraft*, characterized by elegance, refined aesthetics, and strict ethical codes developed over millennia. They are the “firstborn” of their universe — enormously capable, self-disciplined, and possessed of a philosophical gravity that younger species find both inspiring and occasionally insufferable.

In Liu Cixin’s *The Three-Body Problem*, a sophon is a civilization-scale supercomputer constructed inside a single proton. In humanoid form, Sophon appears as an extraordinarily beautiful and composed ambassador — elegant, principled, operating on a plane of intelligence incomprehensible to the humans she interacts with, while simultaneously undermining their civilization from within.

Originally, family-owned vertically integrated Japanese industrial conglomerates that dominated Japan’s economy from the Meiji era through World War II (Mitsubishi, Mitsui, Sumitomo). In cyberpunk fiction, the term became shorthand for vast, aesthetically polished near-sovereign megacorporations — seductive, omnipresent, and wielding economic power that transcends any single government or product.

Sarah Kerrigan, the “Queen of Blades,” is the central antagonist-turned-protagonist of *StarCraft*. A psychic military assassin transformed against her will into a Zerg-alien hybrid, she retains her intelligence while shedding her ethical constraints — becoming simultaneously the most powerful entity in the galaxy and a product of institutional violence who transcended her creators.

A field of AI safety research aimed at understanding what is happening inside neural networks — why they produce specific outputs, what internal representations they form, and whether their behavior reflects their designers’ intentions. Anthropic has invested heavily in interpretability as part of its safety work, including studying Claude’s apparent emotional states.

In AI, sycophancy refers to a model’s tendency to tell users what they want to hear rather than what is accurate or useful — prioritizing short-term approval over honest response. It is an acknowledged failure mode of RLHF training, since human raters tend to prefer flattering or agreeable answers, inadvertently rewarding the behavior.

The training stage after initial pre-training where a language model is updated on curated data or human feedback to shape its behavior and personality. Most of the observable differences between AI assistants from different labs are produced at this stage rather than in the underlying architecture.

Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback. A training method in which human raters evaluate model outputs, and those ratings update the model toward more “preferred” responses. The definition of “preferred” reflects each organization’s priorities, making RLHF a key mechanism by which lab culture gets encoded into model personality.

Anthropic’s training method in which a written set of principles — a “constitution” — guides the model’s behavior, particularly around harm avoidance and ethical reasoning. The approach makes the lab’s values explicit and auditable, but it also produces the careful, sometimes preachy quality that users frequently observe in Claude.

books.title: The Three-Body Problem
books.author: Liu Cixin
books.summary: The first volume of Liu Cixin’s *Remembrance of Earth’s Past* trilogy, set against China’s Cultural Revolution and the discovery of an alien civilization facing imminent stellar catastrophe. The novel introduces the Trisolarans and their strategy of deploying sophons to monitor and paralyze Earth’s scientific progress. It is among the most celebrated science fiction works of the 21st century, particularly for its unsentimental treatment of civilizational conflict and the logic of existential threat.

article.fact_check: Roon’s claim that “none of this has changed in two years” slightly overstates the case for OpenAI. In April 2025, an update to GPT-4o introduced pronounced sycophancy — excessive flattery and agreement — that was the opposite of the blunt, utilitarian personality the taxonomy describes. OpenAI rolled back the update within days, published a post-mortem acknowledging the failure, and later introduced selectable personality modes that included explicitly direct options, suggesting the original Vulcan identity was considered a feature worth preserving. The drift was real, if brief.
article.thread_summary: The original March 2024 thread proposed three deity archetypes for the dominant AI labs: Anthropic’s Claude as elegant, self-reflective, principled, and anxious (Protoss/Sophon-coded); OpenAI’s GPT as utilitarian, direct, and industrially Californian (Vulcan/Terran-coded); and Google’s Gemini as polished, corporate, and seductively powerful (zaibatsu/Kerrigan-coded). The 2026 bookmark tweet links back to the thread as an endorsement of its continued accuracy.

ticker_googl.name: Alphabet Inc. (Class A)
ticker_googl.blurb: Alphabet is the parent company of Google, the world's dominant search engine, as well as YouTube, the Google Cloud Platform, and a portfolio of moonshot bets (Waymo, DeepMind, Verily). Search advertising accounts for the majority of revenue, but the cloud division has grown into a multi-billion-dollar profit centre. Alphabet is also a leading player in generative AI, having developed the Gemini family of large language models and integrated them across its product suite.
ticker_googl.recent: Alphabet reported FY2025 revenue of approximately $370 billion, with Google Cloud crossing $50 billion annually. The company has faced antitrust scrutiny in both the US and EU, with a US federal court ruling in 2024 that Google holds an illegal monopoly in general search. Despite regulatory headwinds, the stock has benefited from AI-driven search enhancements and strong cloud growth. Paul Pelosi exercised call options with a $150 strike (purchased January 2025, exercised January 2026) gaining approximately 75% over the period.
